payload.title: [multi-region-6] FederatingClusterBus inbound path re-injects every cross-region envelope into the local bus wit...
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING multi-region-6 (low/dos, confidence=high, verify-votes +2/-0)

FILE: apps/server/src/cluster/region-bus.ts
LINES: 221-225, 249-251

WHAT: FederatingClusterBus.setSubscribedTenants delegates only to `this.#local.setSubscribedTenants` (line 250), which filters INTRA-region inbound. But envelopes arriving FROM peer regions are unconditionally re-published into the local bus (`this.#region.subscribe((re) => this.#local.publish(re.envelope))`, lines 223-225) regardless of whether this region serves the envelope's tenant. Because re-injection goes through local.publish (the publish path, which is never tenant-filtered — the filter lives on the inbound #onMessage path), every cross-region frame for every tenant is published onto this region's intra-region Redis and only dropped per-node at each node's inbound filter. The bandwidth/CPU saving that setSubscribedTenants was designed to deliver is entirely forfeited for federated traffic: a region serving zero subscribers for tenant T still pays full WAN-receive + full intra-region re-publish for T.

IMPACT: Amplification of cross-region traffic: a region with no interest in a tenant still receives and re-fans every federated envelope for it across its internal Redis to all nodes, inflating WAN+intra-region load and undermining the tenant-filter optimization. Not a correctness break, but a real efficiency/DoS-surface regression at scale.

SUGGESTED FIX: Track the subscribed-tenant set in FederatingClusterBus and short-circuit re-injection of inbound region envelopes whose tenantId is not currently served by this region (skipping the synthetic media-placement sentinel tenant). This mirrors the intra-region filter intent on the federation hop.
